title: The best Google alternative I’ve tried yet
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: Meta Quest 3
recommendations.blurb: It’s not VR anymore, it’s mixed reality. The $499.99 Quest 3 seems to be a big improvement on the Quest 2, and in a brief demo, it showed some pretty solid mixed reality chops. But I’m genuinely curious: do you care about headsets? Are they the future / too early / totally stupid?

recommendations.name: The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar
recommendations.blurb: I love a filmmaking experiment, and this has been a fun one: Wes Anderson made a bunch of short films based on Roald Dahl stories, and they’ve been dropping on Netflix all week. It’s kind of a show, kind of a movie in four parts, kind of an old-fashioned web series? Whatever it is, it’s delightful.

recommendations.name: ChatGPT’s voice commands
recommendations.blurb: Two good things happened to ChatGPT this week: it got back the ability to browse the web in real time, and it became a really handy voice assistant. (You’ll need the $20 a month ChatGPT Plus subscription to get them, at least for now.)

recommendations.name: macOS Sonoma
recommendations.blurb: I include this otherwise relatively straightforward operating system update for one reason and one reason only: the screensavers. Apple basically took those gorgeous, moving screensavers from the Apple TV and ported them to the Mac, and they look so good. Also, you know, widgets and whatever.

recommendations.name: Raspberry Pi 5
recommendations.blurb: There’s still no better computer tinker toy than a Raspberry Pi. The new one, which starts at $60, is a spec upgrade across the board, and it’s as easy as ever to make it a smart home controller / simple media computer / basically anything else you can think of.

recommendations.name: The Creator
recommendations.blurb: This movie has a premise I’m sure you’ve seen a million times before — humans fighting the AI takeover, what does it mean to be human, yadda, yadda, yadda. The Verge’s Charles Pulliam-Moore was left somewhat cold by the movie’s big ideas, but if nothing else, it sounds like totally gorgeous sci-fi.

recommendations.name: The Vivaldi browser
recommendations.blurb: Vivaldi is one of my absolute favorite browsers. It’s superfast, wildly customizable, and as of this week, available just about everywhere! The new iOS app syncs easily with your other browsers, and just like other platforms, has a huge amount of options and features.

recommendations.name: Windows 11’s fall update
recommendations.blurb: Microsoft would tell you the big upgrade this fall is Copilot, its built-in AI assistant for getting things done all over the OS. I’m also into the File Explorer redesign.

recommendations.name: Murder in the 21st
recommendations.blurb: This new show, a true crime series looking at some major investigations and murders through the lens of the victims’ digital footprints, is going to be very popular in my house. It’s the most iconic crossover of my family’s interests since Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce started hanging out.

recommendations.name: Small Web
recommendations.blurb: It’s customizable. Kagi looks a lot like Google and generally feels very similar to use. But unlike Google, Kagi lets you block sites you don’t like and promote sites you do like.

recommendations.name: No ads
recommendations.blurb: The catch with Kagi is you have to pay for it. You get a few searches a month for free, but $10 buys you unlimited access. That’s a lot of money for a search engine! But the pages are so much cleaner and less confusing that I was surprised how quickly I paid up.

recommendations.name: It’s great for videos and podcasts
recommendations.blurb: Podcast search is, like, impossible. But I’ve had surprisingly good luck Kagi-ing topics I’m interested in and finding related podcast episodes, and the engine does a similarly good job of scouring YouTube for interesting stuff.

recommendations.name: Its AI is handy but not in the way
recommendations.blurb: For a lot of queries, Kagi puts a little “Quick Answer” button at the top — click it, and you get a brief AI-generated answer, with cited sources you can click on. That’s exactly the amount of AI I’m looking for in most of my searches.

recommendations.name: Orion
recommendations.blurb: The mobile browser is great. Kagi’s mobile app is a browser called Orion, and it’s as no-frills a mobile browser as you’ll find. But that’s cool by me! It’s fast and easy to use. You can also supposedly download Kagi as a Safari extension on iOS, but I haven’t managed to make that work.

recommendations.name: It seems… good? I’ve tried basically all the search engines, and I usually end u
recommendations.blurb: p back on Google because Google has better results. (Or at least the results I’m expecting and looking for.) With Kagi, I’ve found myself going back to Google less than usual. I don’t know if that’ll hold up forever, but I’m impressed so far.

recommendations.name: A Samsung Galaxy S21 that’s had its life saved many times by a cheapo Amazon pho
recommendations.blurb: The Phone: A Samsung Galaxy S21 that’s had its life saved many times by a cheapo Amazon phone case.

recommendations.name: Baldur’s Gate 3
recommendations.blurb: Baldur’s Gate 3 has awoken one of my primal animating forces: writing fanfiction.

recommendations.name: that meme going around
recommendations.blurb: You know that meme going around about how a lot of women don’t understand how often the men in their lives think about the Roman Empire?

recommendations.name: The screenshot
recommendations.blurb: Epic CEO Tim Sweeney posted a now poorly aged tweet likening Epic to the Roman Empire. ( The screenshot was from a movie and featured Roman soldiers in a forest.

recommendations.name: The Overwatch League
recommendations.blurb: My results were inconclusive.) The Overwatch League.

recommendations.name: Energiza Pro
recommendations.blurb: Energiza Pro, an app for better battery life in the long term. I bought it a few weeks ago. I’m finding it very useful.

recommendations.name: Radio Paradise
recommendations.blurb: Radio Paradise plays an electric mix of music, ad-free, totally free, and has multiple ‘Mixes’ you can listen to (Rock, Mellow, Main, Global). They play a great mix of music I wouldn’t usually listen to, and you can skip the song if you don’t like it.

recommendations.name: Bombas socks
recommendations.blurb: Bombas socks and Kizik shoes. Both the socks and shoes are so comfortable, and the shoes are easy to put on / slip on and off.

recommendations.name: Kizik shoes
recommendations.blurb: Bombas socks and Kizik shoes. Both the socks and shoes are so comfortable, and the shoes are easy to put on / slip on and off.

recommendations.name: Thumper
recommendations.blurb: Recently, I’ve been sucked back into Thumper, one of my favorite games of all time. This playthrough on iOS!

recommendations.name: Z launcher by Nokia
recommendations.blurb: My favorite launcher of all time is the Z launcher by Nokia. It’s been unsupported for a while now and was eventually taken off the app store (breaking my heart). My second favorite launcher, and the one I’m currently using, is Niagara Launcher.

recommendations.name: Niagara Launcher
recommendations.blurb: My favorite launcher of all time is the Z launcher by Nokia. It’s been unsupported for a while now and was eventually taken off the app store (breaking my heart). My second favorite launcher, and the one I’m currently using, is Niagara Launcher.

recommendations.name: Raycast
recommendations.blurb: Raycast! It’s this powerful and modern Spotlight replacement for Mac that’s similar to Alfred but way better and more modern. I use it all day, every day, and it just keeps getting better.

recommendations.name: Death Glitch
recommendations.blurb: I’m really liking Death Glitch by Tamara Kneese about how the social platforms and internet culture handle user death. And obvs, I hear really great things about Kashmir Hill’s new book.

recommendations.blurb: Have you watched Pete Holmes as Badman?

recommendations.name: Troopers
recommendations.blurb: Then, go watch all of “ Troopers,” the fantastic Star Wars parody.

recommendations.name: If Google Was a Guy
recommendations.blurb: “ If Google Was a Guy ” is still one of the funniest tech-related things ever.

recommendations.name: no brandcuffs
recommendations.blurb: I still say “ no brandcuffs ” out loud probably five times a week.

recommendations.name: If All Movies Had Cell Phones
recommendations.blurb: And 14 years later, “ If All Movies Had Cell Phones ” still rings in my ears every time I watch somebody who could absolutely solve all their problems with one text message.
